title: Behind the Screen
blurb: Be the dalang. Listen to the story and move real museum puppets onto the screen.
fact: The dalang does it all: moves every puppet, voices every character, leads the singers and conducts the gamelan, while keeping sound effects with a mallet and his foot.
credit: Source: Behind the Shadows: Javanese Wayang Kulit Puppets in Ramayana and Wayang Kulit (ICH-009), Roots.sg, National Heritage Board. Puppets from the collection of the Asian Civilisations Museum. Narration is computer-generated. Music: Ladrang Wilujeng by Gamelan Nyai Saraswati, CC BY-NC 3.0 US, cut to a loop.

content.intro: Listen to the story. When the big words call for a puppet, drag it from the banana trunk to the glowing mark.

beats.cue: Plant the kayon in the middle
beats.story: The lamp is lit and the gamelan plays. Before any story begins, the kayon, the tree of life, rises in the middle of the screen.
beats.speak: The lamp is lit, and the gamelan plays. Before any story begins, the kah-yon, the tree of life, rises in the middle of the screen.

beats.story: This is the Ramayana. Here walks Prince Rama. His black face tells of his noble line, his downward gaze of a refined nature.
beats.speak: This is the Rah-mah-yah-na. Here walks Prince Rah-ma. His black face tells of his noble line. His downward gaze, of a refined nature.

beats.story: At his side is his wife, Dewi Sinta, eyes lowered, her stance narrow and graceful.
beats.speak: At his side, is his wife, Day-wee Sinta. Eyes lowered. Her stance, narrow and graceful.

beats.story: And never far behind is Lesmana, Rama's loyal brother.
beats.speak: And never far behind, is Les-mah-na, Rah-ma's loyal brother.

beats.story: Then a golden deer appears. It is really Maricha, a demon in disguise, come to lure Rama and Lesmana away from Sinta.
beats.speak: Then a golden deer appears. It is really Mah-ree-cha, a demon in disguise, come to lure Rah-ma and Les-mah-na away from Sinta.

after.story: Rama chases it into the forest. Soon Lesmana goes after him, and Sinta is left alone.
after.speak: Rah-ma chases it into the forest. Soon, Les-mah-na goes after him. And Sinta is left alone.

beats.story: But someone is watching. Rahwana, ogre king of Alengka: blue face, wide eyes, a sneering mouth.
beats.speak: But someone is watching. Rah-wah-na, ogre king of Ah-leng-ka. Blue face. Wide eyes. A sneering mouth.

after.story: Rahwana seizes Sinta and carries her away!
after.speak: Rah-wah-na seizes Sinta, and carries her away!

beats.story: High above, the great bird Jatayu sees it all, and swoops down to fight Rahwana.
beats.speak: High above, the great bird, Jah-tah-yoo, sees it all, and swoops down to fight Rah-wah-na.

after.story: Jatayu falls. With his last breath, he tells Rama and Lesmana that Sinta has been taken.
after.speak: Jah-tah-yoo falls. With his last breath, he tells Rah-ma and Les-mah-na that Sinta has been taken.

beats.cue: Plant the kayon to change the scene
beats.story: The kayon sweeps across the screen. The scene changes, and the story moves on.
beats.speak: The kah-yon sweeps across the screen. The scene changes, and the story moves on.

beats.story: Now, a little laughter. Semar isn't in the Ramayana, but the dalang brings him in to ease the tension, and to give wise advice.
beats.speak: Now, a little laughter. Suh-mar isn't in the Rah-mah-yah-na. But the dah-lahng brings him in, to ease the tension, and to give wise advice.

beats.story: Rama gathers allies. Hanoman, the white monkey, a strong and capable general, joins him.
beats.speak: Rah-ma gathers allies. Ha-no-mahn, the white monkey, a strong and capable general, joins him.

beats.story: Even Wibisana, Rahwana's own brother, turns from Alengka and crosses to Rama's side.
beats.speak: Even Wee-bee-sah-na, Rah-wah-na's own brother, turns from Ah-leng-ka, and crosses to Rah-ma's side.

beats.story: Rahwana's ogres march out to meet them, huge and full of brute force.
beats.speak: Rah-wah-na's ogres march out to meet them. Huge, and full of brute force.

after.story: The battle rages, and Rama's side wins.
after.speak: The battle rages. And Rah-ma's side wins.

beats.story: At last, Sinta is free, and she comes home to Rama.
beats.speak: At last, Sinta is free. And she comes home to Rah-ma.

beats.cue: Plant the kayon to close the night
beats.story: And so the story ends as it began, with the tree of life in the middle of the screen.
beats.speak: And so the story ends as it began. With the tree of life, in the middle of the screen.

figures.caption: Kayon, the Tree of Life or Cosmic Mountain. Placed in the middle of the screen to start or end a show. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-03833.
Rama. His black face shows his noble line; downward gaze, narrow eyes and narrow stance mark him as refined. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, XXXX-05222.
Dewi Sinta. Small eyes, slim nose, downward gaze and narrow stance. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-03892.
Lesmana, Rama's brother. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-04027.

Golden Deer, the demon Maricha in disguise, distracting Rama and Laksmana away from Sita. This one is from Bali, where the same Ramayana is told. Made by Awang Bin Sitai, 1996. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1996-01525.
Rahwana, ruler of Alengka. Blue face, forward-looking gaze, wide-open eyes, sneering mouth and wide stance. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-03936.
Jatayu is a Garuda bird. This Garuda puppet stands in for him. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-03834.
Hanoman, the white monkey and Rama's ally. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-04072.
Wibisana, Rahwana's younger brother, drawn with the features of a refined character. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, 1994-03992.
Ogre. Wide-open eyes, bulbous nose and a grin showing his teeth. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, XXXX-06278.
Semar, chief of the panakawan: comic relief, and wise friends to the noble characters. Java, 20th century. Asian Civilisations Museum, XXXX-05266.

cards.title: Good on the left, bad on the right
cards.text: Puppets wait staked in a banana trunk: good characters on the dalang's left, bad on his right. That's how the trunk at the bottom of the game is laid out.

cards.title: One person, every voice
cards.text: The dalang moves every puppet, voices every character, leads the singers and conducts a gamelan of about 25 musicians.

cards.title: In Singapore
cards.text: Wayang kulit likely came to Singapore with migrants from Java. Today it is performed at festivals, schools and arts venues, and local shows feature heroes like Sang Nila Utama, Hang Nadim and Hang Tuah.

sources.facts: Facts from Behind the Shadows, the Wayang Kulit ICH entry and each puppet's collection listing on Roots.sg, National Heritage Board.
media: Puppet photographs: Asian Civilisations Museum collection, via Roots.sg. Backgrounds removed for the game.

Narration: computer-generated (macOS text-to-speech). Music: Ladrang Wilujeng by Gamelan Nyai Saraswati, recorded live at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2005, CC BY-NC 3.0 US, from the Free Music Archive. Cut to a loop for the game.
